summary.body:
The new slice expression correctly fixes the stated bug: when `n` exceeds `len(items)`, `max(0, len(items) - n)` clamps to `0`, so the full list is returned, matching `items[-n:]`'s behavior in that case.

However, the rewrite silently changes behavior for `n == 0`. `items[-0:]` is equivalent to `items[0:]` (because `-0 == 0` in Python), so the old code returned the **whole list** for `n = 0`. The new code computes `max(0, len(items) - 0) == len(items)`, so `items[len(items):]` returns an **empty list**. That is a behavior change the PR description doesn't mention — it only claims the fix preserves the old slice's behavior and only changes what happens when `n` exceeds the length. If any caller relies on `last_n(items, 0)` returning the full list (however accidental that quirk was), this rewrite breaks it silently.

Relatedly, negative `n` also now behaves differently (e.g. `n = -1`: old code returns `items[1:]`, new code returns `[]`), though that input was already nonsensical/undefined before this change, so it's lower priority.

Recommend either updating the PR description to call out the `n == 0` behavior change explicitly (if intentional), or adjusting the fix to preserve the old `n == 0` result if that matters to callers.

items.markdown: For `n == 0`, this change alters behavior: the old `items[-n:]` (i.e. `items[-0:]` == `items[0:]`) returned the **whole list**, but the new `items[max(0, len(items) - n):]` returns `items[len(items):]`, an **empty list**. The PR's stated intent only covers the case where `n` exceeds the list length ("return the whole list when n exceeds its length, exactly as the slice did") — it says nothing about `n == 0`, so this is an unannounced behavior change for that edge case.
items.trailer: Confirm whether any caller depends on `last_n(items, 0)` returning the full list, and if so, adjust the fix (or explicitly document the behavior change) rather than silently altering it.
